title: Families of sets
public: a family is an indexed collection of sets

exercises.title: Define a family of subsets
exercises.objective: Represent an indexed family as a function into Set α.
success: a family is an indexed collection of sets

exercises.title: Express closure under unions
exercises.objective: Quantify over every subfamily, not only binary unions.
success: union closure applies to every subfamily

exercises.title: Express binary intersection closure
exercises.objective: Require every pairwise intersection to remain in the family.
success: binary intersection closure applies to every pair

exercises.title: Separate finite and arbitrary closure
exercises.objective: Exhibit a finite-intersection-closed family with a missing arbitrary union.
success: the finite family is binary intersection closed

checks.lean: example : T2.Family Nat Bool → Set Nat := fun f => f true
checks.message: A `Family Nat Bool` must be applied to a `Bool` index to produce a `Set Nat`.

checks.lean: example {α : Type*} (C : Set (Set α)) (h : T2.ClosedUnderUnions C) : ∅ ∈ C := by simpa using h ∅ (by simp)
checks.message: Arbitrary-union closure must include the empty union: apply your definition to the empty subfamily.

checks.lean: example {α : Type*} : Set (Set α) → Prop := T2.ClosedUnderUnions
example {α : Type*} : Set (Set α) → Prop := T2.ClosedUnderBinaryIntersections

steps: The index type is the domain; `Set α` is the codomain.
Take an arbitrary `D : Set (Set α)`. Which assumption relates it to `C`?
hints.hint: Use `∀ D : Set (Set α), D ⊆ C → ⋃₀ D ∈ C`.
Use `∀ s ∈ C, ∀ t ∈ C, s ∩ t ∈ C`.
Use exactly `{∅, {0}, {1}, Set.univ}`. Any two distinct singleton sets meet in `∅`.
